notes.text: D-007 (see decisions.md) fixes the shape of the draw: weight a candidate cell by pow(scent, k) with a tunable exponent k slightly above 1, never exp(k*scent) — at the 0-500 scale from PEO-026 exp saturates immediately. A power law keys off the ratio between neighbouring cells, so one k stays decisive next to the player and becomes a gentle drift far away, which is the horde-drift behaviour the user asked for. Fold this into the brief when PEO-009 is planned.

The Dead do not converge within 3 s: scent spreads ~8 cells in 20 s, so distant Dead never move

notes.text: Raised D-007 (scent reach / convergence pacing). Blocked on the pacing answer: the front-radius test in this brief can only pin a number once the target reach is chosen. Technical instrumentation is ready to write behind the decision.

D-007 answered and recorded in decisions.md; briefed. Root cause identified from the code: the ~8-cell reach is the floor flush in scent.cpp (v < floor -> 0.0F, floor 0.001F against a 1.0F deposit); past it the field is exactly zero, strongest_neighbour requires v > best strictly, so distant Dead never move. Fix is dynamic range, not diffusion rate.

Brief corrected: kPlayerScent already exists at src/app/main.cpp:26 as 1.0F, so the unit raises it rather than introducing it. Starting tuning values (diffusion 0.8, decay 0.01, floor 1e-6) are carried over from branch claude/fervent-curie-iqonhg, which reached the same numbers independently; that branch's pinning test asserted only sample > 0.0F against a 1e-6 floor, which passes on the tail crossing rather than a usable scent level, so the tests here assert a strictly decreasing gradient and actual Dead convergence instead.

Re-briefed against measured data. Two corrections to my earlier brief: the acceptance test I wrote was unsatisfiable (at 200 steps the front reaches 45 cells, and I asserted at 62 — sample was exactly 0.0), and diffusion 0.8 is in the oscillatory regime. Verified replacements are in the units. Separately, D-008 now covers the finding that a moving player outruns their own scent entirely, which this item cannot fix.

Do not start this before the wall-absorption item (order 255). That change alters the field's shape, so both the retune constants and the test parameters in these units — which were measured on an open grid with reflecting edges — must be re-derived afterwards. Ask the Architect to re-measure rather than guessing new numbers.
starting; re-deriving test numbers after PEO-029
All units landed, tests pass. GOAL NOT MET in game: with absorbing walls, steady-state reach is 29 cells; 28/40 Dead in peo 7 never move. Numbers in report commit; needs a decision.

review: rework. Units are correct; the goal is not met, and no decision is needed to meet it. Reach goes as lambda * ln(peak/floor) (D-007): at floor 1e-6 the field is cut off at 25-29 cells. Architect probe, World defaults, 300 waits: seeds 7/1/42 give reach 29/25/27 and 12/12/11 of 40 Dead moving; with floor 1e-30 reach is 77 (whole map) and 40/40 move on all three. 1. ScentParams::floor default 1e-6 -> 1e-30. Comment why, and why not lower: it must stay well above FLT_MIN (1.18e-38) so step never touches subnormals. 2. Add 'every Dead moves when the player waits' to test_world.cpp on the small stage (24x16, default scent params, 300 waits or fewer if the suite budget needs it): every unit's position has changed. Measure its time with -d. 3. docs/design/scent-mobs.md:74 claims 'a gradient reaches the map edge' at floor 1e-6; correct it to the new floor and state it for real stages with absorbing walls. 4. Re-run the in-game manual steps from the brief and report the counts. The pinned bit-pattern test sets floor 1e-6 explicitly and needs no change. D-010 (scent buildup) is separate and lands in PEO-030; do not start it here.

items.title: Two-layer staggered scent field: near layer each turn, far layer by IIR

notes.text: D-010 (2026-09-29): the far layer becomes a buildup layer. A cell's fade rate falls as the sliding 3x3 box total around it rises, to a nonzero minimum; box totals refresh on a turn schedule (every turn near the player, staggered further out); buildup pulls harder than a fresh trail. The separable IIR solve assumes a single decay everywhere, so re-examine the method (e.g. a coarse FTCS far layer stepped on a stagger) when briefing. Acceptance adds: a den where the player lingered, and a path walked often, both outlast and outpull a fresh trail.
